hook.text: A user in Tokyo calls your API hosted in Virginia. The round trip adds 200 milliseconds of lag.

buildup.text: Edge functions run your code on servers distributed worldwide — close to each user, not in one region.

discovery.text: Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge Functions, and Deno Deploy are popular edge compute platforms.

twist.text: Edge functions have limits: smaller memory, shorter runtimes, and restricted access to databases.

climax.text: For personalization, authentication, and redirects, edge functions are transformatively fast.

punchline.text: Run code where your users are, not where your data center is.

quiz.question: What is the main benefit of edge functions?
options: Running code geographically close to users for lower latency
Storing data permanently at the edge of the network
Replacing all cloud data centers with local computers

details.summary: Edge functions run serverless code at CDN edge locations closest to users, reducing latency to single-digit milliseconds. Cloudflare Workers, AWS Lambda@Edge, and Vercel Edge Functions execute logic like authentication, A/B testing, and personalization at the network edge.
details.whyItMatters: Edge computing brings logic closer to users, enabling instant responses for latency-sensitive operations without round-trips to origin servers in distant regions.
takeaways: Code runs at CDN edge locations nearest the user
Single-digit millisecond response times for edge logic
Ideal for authentication, routing, and personalization

faq.question: How do edge functions differ from regular serverless?
faq.answer: Regular serverless runs in specific cloud regions. Edge functions run at CDN edge locations distributed globally, executing closer to users. They typically have tighter resource constraints but offer dramatically lower latency for geographically distributed users.

faq.question: What are common edge function use cases?
faq.answer: URL rewriting, authentication and authorization checks, A/B testing, geolocation-based content, bot detection, request header manipulation, and API response caching are all common. Any lightweight logic that benefits from user proximity fits edge functions.
